# Server context: cestmoi

_Generated by **moi** from the live machine, state as of **2026-11-26T17:00:00Z**. Regenerated after every snapshot (within minutes of a change, and daily) and after every audit. Do not edit this file: describe things with `sudo moi notes`._

## How to use this document (for AI assistants)
- This is the ground truth for what runs on this server as of the timestamp above. If something matters, verify it live (`docker ps`, `systemctl status`, `crontab -l`).
- Before proposing a change, check it against what is here: **ports in use, Docker network names and subnets, bind-mount paths, volume names, schedules, firewall rules, disk space**.
- Keep changes reproducible so they are captured and can be rebuilt: containers go in a compose file inside an existing stack directory (see Docker), scripts in a captured script directory, services as units in `/etc/systemd/system`, jobs via `crontab`, and **health checks, backups and monitors in `/etc/moi/moi.toml`** (validate with `moi config check`). Avoid one-off `docker run` and edits outside these places.
- After making changes: `sudo moi snapshot` (it also happens by itself within minutes), then record the *why* with `sudo moi notes`.
- Secrets are redacted (`***`, push tokens as `…last4`). The real values are in the files named here, on the server, readable by root only.
- Raw data: `/var/lib/moi/state/snapshot/` (configs, compose files, normalized Docker state). History: `sudo moi log`, `sudo moi diff`.

## moi
Version <version> · configuration `/etc/moi/moi.toml` (secrets in `secrets.toml`, never printed here) · state `/var/lib/moi`.

### Health checks (which check feeds which monitor)
| Check | Every | Uptime Kuma monitor | Journal tag |
|---|---|---|---|
| resources | 5m | Server Resources | resource-check |
| storage | 5m | Server Storage | storage-check |
| services | 5m | Server Internal Services | service-check |
| edge | with services | Server Internal Services |  |
`services` runs 17 HTTP and 4 exec probes; change them in `[checks.services]`, not in scripts.
- **Backup**: daily at `03:30` to `/mnt/storage/backups` (kept 7d, at most 20GB), off-site with restic (tag `nightly`, at most one upload per 20h, prune on Sun). Monitor: Server Backup.
- **Self-healing rules**: `traefik-homelab`, `traefik-config-guard`, `vpn-stack`.
- **Boot**: waits for `/mnt/storage`, then starts the stacks in `/opt/services/**`, `/opt/yams`; verifies after 4m.
- **Firewall**: moi owns the chains INPUT, DOCKER-USER (rules in `/etc/moi/firewall/rules4.txt` and `/etc/moi/firewall/rules6.txt`) and applies them at boot; Docker owns the rest.
- **Monitors**: Uptime Kuma at http://uptime.home (live mode). moi adopts existing monitors by name and push token and never recreates them.

## Firewall & access control

### iptables (filter table, without Docker's generated chains and ufw/fail2ban internals)
```
:INPUT DROP
:FORWARD DROP
:DOCKER-USER -
:f2b-sshd -
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p tcp -m multiport --dports 22 -j f2b-sshd
-A FORWARD -j DOCKER-USER
-A DOCKER-USER -m comment --comment "Intra-network container traffic" -j RETURN
-A DOCKER-USER -m comment --comment "Swarm outbound Internet" -j RETURN
-A DOCKER-USER -j DROP
```
_Custom DOCKER-USER rules exist: they filter traffic to published container ports._
**sshd:** passwordauthentication=no
